title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from neighbouring pages): over a base S (eventually Spec Z, the 'absolute modular case'), G = GL2 and PG = PGL2. The elements rho (order 6) and sigma (order 4) of SL2(Z) have centralizer tori T_rho and T_sigma; for sigma this is cσ+d, essentially the Weil restriction of G_m from Z[i]. Here sigma^2 = v with v invertible (v = -1 for sigma of order 4), so det(cσ+d) = d^2 - v c^2 and (cσ+d)^2 = v c^2 + d^2 + 2cd σ. N'_sigma is the normalizer-type group {g : gσg^{-1} = ±σ}, with N'_sigma/T_sigma ≅ μ2 given by the sign. The prefix S means the det = 1 part; S' means the det^2 = 1 part. M_{rho,sigma} is a group scheme with a homomorphism Θ̃: M_{rho,sigma} → PG whose kernel is R_{rho,sigma} ≅ S'T_rho × SN'_sigma × G_m (eq. (124)-(126) of the previous page). R_{rho,sigma} commutes with SG and M = R·SG.

This page computes the centre of M_{rho,sigma}.

(i) The centre maps into Cent(PGL2) = 1, so Cent(M) ⊂ Ker Θ̃ = R.

(ii) Since R commutes with SG and R·SG = M, an element of R is central in M iff it is central in R. Hence (128): Cent(M) = Cent(R) = S'T_rho × Cent(SN'_sigma) × G_m, the first and last factors being commutative.

(iii) To compute Cent(SN'_sigma), he observes that μ2 = N'/T acts faithfully on T_sigma = G_m·ST_sigma, hence on ST_sigma, by Galois conjugation (on ST_sigma this is x ↦ x^{-1}). He concludes (129): Cent(SN'_sigma) ⊂ ST_sigma, hence equals the fixed points (ST_sigma)^{μ2}.

(iv) A first, struck-out attempt bounded the centre by the 2-torsion of ST_sigma. Writing g = cσ+d with det g = 1 and g^2 = 1 gives 2vc^2 = 0, 2cd = 0, d^2 - vc^2 = 1. When 2 is invertible this yields c = 0, d^2 = 1, i.e. g ∈ μ2. In residue characteristic 2 the 2-torsion is much larger.

(v) He abandons this and writes (131): Cent(SN'_sigma) = (ST_sigma)^{μ2} = ST_sigma ∩ G_m = μ2. He strikes both the restriction 'si 2 inv. sur S' and a remark that in general one only has μ2 ⊂ Cent with an isomorphism on geometric fibres. The next page concludes, with 'je crois', that Cent(M) ≅ S'T_rho × μ2 × G_m (dimension 2), and evaluates on Z-points: Z/6 × {±1} × {±1}.

Purpose: in the study of the loop equation / modular group (SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6), this determines the centre of the group scheme M_{rho,sigma} attached to the pair (rho, sigma), integrally over Z.
errors: The faithfulness argument alone does not give Cent(SN'_sigma) ⊂ ST_sigma. The cleaner reason is that σ ∈ ST_sigma(Z) is a regular (cyclic) matrix on every fibre, including at 2, so its centralizer in GL2 is exactly T_sigma scheme-theoretically. Then Cent ⊂ T_sigma ∩ SN' = ST_sigma.

At the prime 2, T_sigma is not a torus (Z[i] is ramified at 2), so the 'torus' language and the identification (ST_sigma)^{μ2} = ST_sigma ∩ G_m need care. The equality still holds scheme-theoretically. The μ2-action is (c,d) ↦ (εc,d); requiring c(ε-1) = 0 for all points ε of μ2, including infinitesimal ones, forces c = 0.

Point (v) of the reconstruction assumes SN'_sigma → μ2 is an fppf epimorphism, including onto the infinitesimal μ2 at 2. This is not checked. If it failed, the centre could be larger in characteristic 2: on reduced points over F̄2, SN' coincides with the commutative ST_sigma. This explains Grothendieck's hesitation ('je crois' on the next page).
In the struck computation, the defining condition of the 2-torsion is written '...=0' where g^2 = 1 requires 'v c^2 + d^2 + 2cdσ = 1'. It is corrected in the next line.

ideas.what: Centre of an extension M = R·SG with R commuting with SG and the centre of the image PG trivial: Cent(M) = Cent(R)
ideas.modern_name: centre of a central product / centralizer computation for group schemes
ideas.where_published: general techniques in SGA 3; this specific group M_{rho,sigma} unsure

ideas.what: Centre of the normalizer of the anisotropic norm-one torus attached to σ (order 4) equals μ2, computed scheme-theoretically over Z including at 2
ideas.modern_name: centre of the normalizer of a non-split (ramified at 2) torus in SL2 over Z; fixed points of a μ2-action
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard over fields; integral version folklore

deep.surprise_reason: Routine computation of a centre of a group scheme. The only point of interest is Grothendieck's visible hesitation about the prime 2, which resolves positively scheme-theoretically under a flatness/surjectivity assumption. Nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line after (129) on the right: 'donc μ2 ≃ SN'_σ/T_σ opère fidèlement sur ST_σ' (the subscript under ≃ is '21'/'≀' as transcribed). Mathematically the quotient should be SN'_σ/ST_σ.
In the struck block, the defining set for ₂(ST_σ) is written in the image as '{cσ+d | -vc²+d²=1, vc²+d²+2σcd=0}', with '=0' as written by Grothendieck (should be =1).

Final (131): the image reads 'Cent(SN'_σ) = [struck ST_σ] (ST_σ)^{μ2} = ST_σ ∩ G_m [struck: si 2 inv. sur S]', followed by 'd'où' above. The struck tail is followed by a struck 'Dans le cas général on aura seulement'.
'd'où évidemment' at the top is likely 'd'où évidemment' overwritten; the header '525' is Grothendieck's own page number.
